utterances.text: So this period between April and maybe June, let us say, marked a new phase in the country. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I think it is a convenient time to break for lunch.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: The Trial Chamber will rise and reassemble at 2.30. (Luncheon Adjournment) 24 25 (2.30 pm) JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: The witness is continuing on oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Please, Dr Calic, will you pick up your statement again and conclude your statement for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. To continue, I would like briefly to summarise what I was saying before the break about the political and military structures in Konjic in April, May 1992. I prepared a diagram. This is document number 50. Just to make it a bit clearer, can we have it on the screen, please? It should be reduced a bit. It has to be reduced. We cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Will you please reduce it a bit, if possible. There we are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. This diagram was made by myself. It shows defence planning or military planning, security planning in Konjic municipality as of May 1992. I mentioned the War Presidency as the highest administrative, highest political body in this municipality and I mentioned on the military side the two main military actors. HVO, the Croat military, and the Bosnian Army speaks for itself. The two were related. They had a joint command. They were acting together. We are not completely sure whether or not the members of the two structures participated in the War Presidency. If they were official members under the old Bosnian law there was a representative from the HVO participating in the War Presidency; under the new law he was not, but maybe we can assume close contacts, frequent meetings and maybe even joint decisions because, of course, the work of the War Presidency and the work of the military was interrelated and defence could not function otherwise. In the middle we have the very wide position of the co-ordinator, trying to coordinate the civilian military sides. Again I do not know exactly what his functions were but there was certainly a necessity to coordinate the different activities at this stage. The relationship between the Bosnian Army and the Croat army, the HVO actually, were a bit disturbed by some disputes. I mentioned earlier this morning the fact that the Croats were trying to establish their own community the Herceg-Bosna community as a political community but also having their own army, the HVO. There were disputes arising around this, coming to a head in July 1992. This led, in fact, to a split of this joint command. Completely separate structures were then established by July 1992. There was then de facto a period where parallel power structures existed, Croat and Muslim power structures in the same municipalities, and again they were formally allied and they were continuing to act together, as they were doing in other areas of Bosnia and Herzegovina. In the summer of 1992 also the Bosnian government was more successful in establishing state structures and also in streamlining the military, and this led to the establishment of a new administrative structure on the republican level, and it led to a reorganisation of the Bosnian Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before, Dr Calic, we leave this organogram you made with the co-ordinator, in the middle, we know in this case there was indeed a co-ordinator in Konjic. Can you say something if this was usual in other municipalities that also have a similar structure that they also have a co-ordinator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can say on the diagram I showed before lunchtime that coordination was necessary and also coordination was needed in many instances, and also the statutory of all people's defence had in mind to have these coordinating functions. If there was a position of only one co-ordinator or if there were several, this was, of course, then up to the authorities or to the actors on the ground. It depended also on the real needs, on the concrete circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have seen it also in other municipalities or structures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not seen it in exactly the same way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In August 1997, seven regional administrators of districts within Bosnia and Herzegovina were formed by the BH government. Konjic was designated to form part of the regional district of Mostar. Just to remind you of where Mostar is located, so we have the municipality of Konjic, Mostar is kind of the capital of the region of Herzegovina. So Konjic was supposed to be a part of the district of the -- of the Mostar district. I have got a document about this. This is document number 56, the decree on the establishment and the functioning of districts. These districts were authorised to organise and to prepare citizens for defence, for armed struggle on the territory of the distinct. This included also that many duties that were formally fulfilled by the War Presidencies in the municipalities moved to these regional centres. The new district structures were, therefore, in a position to potentially reduce the local powers of the municipalities and again we do not know whether or not or when this law was implemented. It was published in August, but if they managed to efficiently implement this law is not known to me. As for the military reorganisation of the army, I have another diagram, document 57. It shows the composition of the Bosnian Army at the end of 1992, when this was produced by UN sources. Five corps were established. You can see them on this diagram. The military of Konjic was subordinated to the fourth corps with an HQ in Mostar. I was showing earlier this day how the Bosnian government was trying to establish this HQ in Mostar but it did not work at this time but later in 1992 they were then successful in establishing this HQ and the fourth corps was established with its headquarters in Mostar. This fourth corps commanded all army units of Mostar of Jablinica and other areas, Prozor, including also parts of the formerly-mentioned tactical group 1, which had dissolved by this stage. What happened after the end of 1992? The relations between the Croats and the Muslims or between the HVO and the Bosnian Army got worse and worse. There arose conflicts between the BH armed forces and the HVO. Already in the autumn of 1992 in some parts of Central Bosnia including Konjic, and they intensified during 1993, and they were ended as late as early 1994. They thus created a kind of second war. The people call it second war between Muslim and Croat armed forces, between the BH army and the HVO. To conclude, I wish to show you how Konjic -- the ethnic composition of Konjic looks like today exactly in September -- how it looked like in September 1996. This is based on data from the UNHCR in this area. The respective report of UNHCR is also included in this binder. It is document 58. Konjic municipality today belongs to the federation of Bosnia, under the Dayton Agreement has two parts. The Serb republic on the one hand and the federation on the other hand, so Konjic municipality today forms part of the federation. The composition as of September 1996 is the following. We have 88 per cent Muslims; we have 4 per cent Croats; 2 per cent Serbs; and 6 per cent others. More than 18,000 people left the municipality during the war, but there were coming new people, refugees and displaced persons, so this also, of course, changed the ethnic structure of this municipality, and very few persons have managed to return. There are only 270 Muslims returned and only 14 Serbs have managed to return to their homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only how many?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 14 persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 14 Serbs have returned by September 1996. I would like to conclude with this diagram showing how much the ethnic structure changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Dr Calic, for this comprehensive and also very detailed and fact-filled presentation of yours. I have no questions to ask and I have concluded my examination of Dr Calic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Excuse me. I want to ask a question. I do not know whether it is really relevant or not. You are talking about ethnic compositions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You have Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Serbs. Do they come from different stocks or is it just a difference in religion that is important?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are basically of the same ethnic stock. They are all south Slavs. They had historically -- historically they belonged to different religions. The Serbs are Orthodox religion, Muslims, Islam and both Croats were Catholic. During the 1970s these religious communities were transformed into nations. People got national consciousness and they perceived themselves as being nations. So we have the fact that the religious communities were effectively transformed into people, into nations. People perceived themselves as belonging to a nation more than belonging to a religious community. Many persons are not religious at all. So we have to recognise that these people are now nations and not religious communities any more. JUDGE ODIO BENITO: I am sorry. In the same line I would like to know if the same happened with the Jews, because in the list of the ethnic composition you gave to us, the same that the Muslims, you also -- not you -- the document listed Jews among the Turks, Italians, Slovenians and so it is the same. They are a nationality; they are not a religious group.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is again a matter of debate, whether the Jews form a nation or whether they belong to a religious community. In Yugoslavia the law was that they formed an ethnic group, a minority. They were not recognised as a constituent people of Yugoslavia. As constituent nations of Yugoslavia were recognised only six nations. The Slovenians, Croats, Bosnian Muslims, Serbs, Montenegrans and Macedonians. All other peoples were considered as minorities. They had certain rights but they were not considered as constituent nations of Yugoslavia. JUDGE ODIO BENITO: It is a little complex?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is very complex. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Actually your interpretation gives me some anxiety. You start with a general concentration of Bosnia as the nation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: But within it you come up with Muslims and Serbs. From your explanation you say they all come from the same stock?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Historically. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 6th century -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: How do you now get other nations which are within that general umbrella of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. I did not get the question. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: How do you get other nations within the general umbrella of Bosnia, which is the main stock?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are historically belonging to the same South Slavic stock, tribes coming to the Balkans in about the 6th century. They were then dividing, because they got different religions. By getting different religions, they were also getting different nationalities. They speak basically the same language. They can understand each other easily. There are, of course, different variants and different dialects, but they perceived themselves as belonging to different nations. Again it is very complex and a difficult thing to explain, but I think we should accept that these persons perceived themselves as belonging to a nation. Even if they all live together in the same country, in Bosnia, but they are different nations. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I do not know. I think I do not rationalise, because it does not appear those who have considered religion as a binding tie have considered themselves a different nation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a specific historical development in South-eastern Europe. It is very specific to this area. One reason for this is that this area was for quite a long time, for many centuries, under foreign rule, and these people had practically no rights to participate in the rule of the foreigners, but shed certain cultural rights, and these cultural rights were concentrated in the religious communities and the churches. So the churches became maybe the most important agent of forming national consciousness, and this is how they developed. In the 19th century they were aware that they were different and this is how was created then this perception of being a nation, forming a nation. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Any questions from the defence? Any cross-examination? MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, the defence would like to inform you that the cross-examination of this witness will be conducted in the following way. First, the defence counsel for Zejnil Delalic will question, followed by Hazim Delic's defence counsel. Following that the defence counsel for Esad Landzo and as a fourth the witness will be questioned by the defence counsel for Zdravko Mucic. Mr President, since I am starting cross-examination and I have some documents here, would you allow me to move over to that lectern? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You can do so, please. Cross-examination by MS RESIDOVIC MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Ms Calic, first I would like to ask you which pronunciation is correct: Calic not Calick, since I have heard both variants of your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can call me Calic, because this is my father's name because this is my father's name but I was born in Germany and the Germans for some mysterious reasons eliminated the diacritics. Maybe it is difficult for them to pronounce. You can of course call me Calic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would not want to mispronounce your name, so I will call you Ms Calic. Before we received your report with the voluminous binder, the defence counsel also received information from the prosecution regarding experts that they will use for expert witnesses in these proceedings. In this information it was indicated that you were to present a historical, political and military context and circumstances surrounding the violations of the international humanitarian law as stipulated in the indictment and the national, municipal and historical circumstances in the Konjic region. Given that in your presentation there is no chapter addressing the historical context, I would like to request that you answer several questions, that is to confirm possibly some facts on which the introductory parts of the indictment are based. So these are my questions: is it true, Ms Calic, that Bosnia-Herzegovina as a state has roots in history of over 1,000 years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosnia as a state existed in the Middle Ages, but then in 1463 it was conquered by the Turks, and I would not say that there is a continuity of state from the Middle Ages until today, because there are many centuries in between. Bosnia has, of course, a long history, but it has also a history of foreign rule.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you agree that other states that existed in the Middle Ages in the Balkans shared the same fate, that for a significant historical period of time they were also occupied by other foreign rules? Turning to Bosnia, could you testify before this Trial Chamber that, except for the period during the kingdom of Yugoslavia, when there were certain districts called banjabina and during the fascist state of Croatia during World War II, the territorial form of Bosnia-Herzegovina existed, regardless of the foreign rule in that region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's difficult to say "yes" in this case, because the administrative borders were changing, and you mentioned the Croat state of the Second World War and you mentioned the first Yugoslavia. I mean, these are also historical periods to be taken into consideration, and I just would not like, being a historian myself, to draw this line of continuity from the Middle Ages until today, because then we have to do the same with other nations, with the Serbs and the Croats, and the borders were overlapping, and we really getting into big troubles. I think we should accept that Bosnia was recognised as an independent state in the borders of the Republic of Bosnia, one of the republics of the former Yugoslavia. It was a recognised state and I think this is also enough to know for this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Ms Calic, I think you will agree if I say that the specific historical events after 1990 cannot be properly understood without knowledge of a preceding period? Can I bring you back to more recent history. The Zavnobih conference in 1942, Bosnia was defined as one constituent part of the new Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- have you answered that, just for the record, please? These decisions were also confirmed by Abnoj, which was the top legislative body during World War II. Can you confirm that these borders are the borders of Bosnia-Herzegovina just prior to the outbreak of the war? Taking into account certain historical facts, I would like to ask whether you know that in Bosnia-Herzegovina different populations have lived there with a large amount of tolerance for centuries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you also confirm to me, Ms Calic, that in the document of 1463, which is an edict on religious freedoms and one of the oldest documents on religious freedom in Europe issued by Mehmed Fatih and entitled "Ahdnama" which was directed to the Franciscan monks in Bosnia and is still kept in Fojnica in a Franciscan monastery, it has been unequivocally determined that Jewish, Orthodox, Catholic members within Bosnia-Herzegovina can work freely and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to look at this document before I confirm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, you are not familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to see the document right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not in a position -- I just wanted to know whether I knew of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to verify it before I confirm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not in a position to show it to you today but I will be in a position to show it to the tribunal, but the point is that you were not able to see it today and so you cannot speak to it. However, your knowledge of Bosnia should point to the significant religious tolerance within Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, in your presentation you said that a large part of the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina is mixed in ethnic terms. Is it true if I said that there is no municipality in Bosnia-Herzegovina and there are 109 of them in which there are no -- there are -- in which all constituent populations in Bosnia-Herzegovina are not represented including Jewish and other minorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I have to verify it. We have all the statistical documentation in this book, and I think if this is necessary for the case, you just mention the municipalities, and we verify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can show you an official document indicating that there is no such municipality. However, I would like you to turn to your document number 3 -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Will counsel kindly take into consideration the interpreters and go a little slowly so that they can interpret perfectly. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Can we please show document number 3, representing the ethnic map of the former SFRY and which -- it comes from a source from the -- Republic of Croatia according to you. If I can show the green colour in your map is the territory where -- populated by the Serbs; is that correct? Ms Calic, do you believe that this could be a correct ethnic map of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It cannot be a complete correct map of Bosnia and Herzegovina because nobody would understand it any more. The ethnic make-up of this republic is so complex and the nations are settled so intermixed you would simply not understand any more where the majority areas are. So in this sense you are right. This is not a correct map of the ethnic composition of Bosnia before the war. It is a reduction of facts. It is just to make visible that there were certain areas where certain people were in a majority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, does that mean that this map represents -- is a misrepresentation of the ethnic distribution of the population of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it's not a false description. It is just a reduction of facts, of very complex facts, and I agree on that, that each reduction -- wherever you try to reduce very complex facts, you try to make them visible, they, of course, may contain some incorrectness. It is just to make it visible to help us to understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, this reduction of the ethnic map of Bosnia and Herzegovina to a person who is not familiar with Bosnia-Herzegovina would entitle a people that its ethnic division was actually possible. Would you please show me on this map where Banja Luka is situated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have a map of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It will be wrong. I prefer to use the map where we can all see where Banja Luka is situated. It is document 38. We have Banja Luka here and Konjic is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I am interested in Banja Luka, because in your map it is in the green area, where it would show that it is Serb populated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All these colours, of course, indicate kind of majority areas. There were, of course, settling other people. This is just a way of presenting. Of course, there are other ways of presenting. We have also then other mistakes, as you would call it. I would agree that you show another map which is more correct or which is able to show us all how the ethnic composition of Bosnia was at that time. I would very much agree on this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, you offered this map as proof of the ethnic composition of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Please if the Banja Luka municipality has 195,000 population and over 51 per cent of them are non-Serbs, is it not then incorrect to show the area --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Dr Calic, may I ask you not to answer the question until the translation of Madam Residovic's question is over to here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry. I use the translation maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: So we are able to understand you. We know you understand Serbo-Croat. We others do not. MS RESIDOVIC (in translation): I apologise, your Honour. I will only bring up two more examples to prove that this document, however accurately it depicts the reduced picture it is an absolutely inaccurate picture of the ethnic population of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Ms Calic, could you show us on this map where the Bijeljina municipality is located? It is also in the green area and the official data say in this area there is no Serb majority living. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to stress again that this is a very simplified way of showing the very complex ethnic mix-up of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I would encourage you to present a map which would be able to show us in a more correct way how people were living together. I was unfortunately unable on an A4 paper to provide a better map. I agree if we could have a big map and then we could also go in more details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, I would only like to ask whether this map can represent the ethnic map of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that it is a correct map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a simplified map made to help us understand how the situation was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is incorrect. Ms Calic, this map does not give an opportunity to see the complexity of the situation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were many villages in Bosnia, ethnically mixed. If we would try to show each of these villages in its concrete mixture by colours, I think it would be very difficult. I think it is impossible to show this. It is a simplified way of showing a very complex situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that would be the only true representation, would it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would have indicated the accurate precise data in each municipality and in each village, that would be the accurate representation of the ethnic composition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I provided statistical data for every village in the Konjic municipality. They are included in this file. I did not provide them for all the municipalities of Bosnia. I did not consider that it would be relevant to this case, but, of course, we can provide the statistics, the population census of 1991, and then we will also have the exact numbers, figures of people, of nations in any village, but as for Konjic, all villages are included here. We have exact figures of 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise, Ms Calic, but could you answer me on the situation in Bjeljina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to verify the data before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean, Ms Calic, that for Bosnia and Herzegovina to which you are testifying, you do not have accurate data at this time and you cannot speak to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have accurate data upstairs, and I, of course, can provide them, if you give me the time, but there were 20 nations and nationalities, and if you ask me how many of each of these nationalities were living in a certain municipality, I have to verify it before, I am afraid, and yes -- yes, this is what I want to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, is it 20 nationalities who lived in every municipality and every part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a single municipality in Bosnia-Herzegovina in which -- where at least one member of one of the nationalities was not also part of the inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question. I was listening to the English translation. I did not understand. Can you repeat, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please could you indicate a single municipality in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina where members of any of the nationalities did not live or the reverse, where only a single population lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Municipalities? No, I could not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a document here which is an official document, not verified. It is a statistical document. May I show this to Ms Calic, please? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You can show it to her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You will have to exhibit it then. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes. That is the purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mr Ostberg, you will have to exhibit this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: After the cross-examination, your Honour, I will introduce all of it. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Show it to the witness. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I would like to show the document just for the cross-examination purposes, and as we are going to call our own expert witnesses, they will offer their own documents in the proceedings later. Ms Calic, have you had a chance to look at this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen a similar statistical report before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have not, and I do not know from where it comes. It is a fax, the numbers, figures. I don't know on which basis it has been made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of a population census of 1991 by the official institution, that is the Statistical Institute of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but if you have not seen it, I cannot expect you to comment on it. Therefore, you cannot answer my question and that is: is there a single municipality in Bosnia-Herzegovina inhabited by members of a single nation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I rely on the population census of 1991. I have never seen it in this form. I have never seen it in a faxed form. I have seen it in a form of a book. This is why I have just to compare the figures. This comes from a different institution. This comes from the Obernistic Institute of Sarajevo. I got the figures from the statistic office in Sarajevo. Please give me the opportunity just to compare these figures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I should like to go back now, Ms Calic, to the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I would like to ask you kindly to confirm once again that Bosnia-Herzegovina, in accordance with the decisions of Zabnobih and Avnoj was constituted as an equal republic of first the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and later SFRY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the constitution of 1974, Article 3 of the constitution of 1974, stipulates the republics as "states"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact term, if it was "state".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I read the text for you as it is in your documentation: "Article 3. The socialist -- a socialist republic is a state based on the sovereignty of the nations and the authority and self-management of the working class and all working people."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But the word "state" is not mentioned in this? The word state is not mentioned in this Article.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The socialist republic is a state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. I did not get those words.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you also confirm that this constitution in Article 5 stipulates that the territory of the republic cannot be changed without the agreement of the republic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can confirm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your view that Bosnia and Herzegovina was a state like all the other republics within the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It had an equal status and it was recognised as an independent republic in April 1992 in the existing borders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, in your testimony you said, and I quote: "The Muslim leadership aspired towards preserving Bosnia-Herzegovina as a unified, multi-ethnic unit Aryan state." Did you make this assessment on the basis of a document of some kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did make this statement on the basis of many Articles, of many speeches which were made by Bosnian leaders, by party leaders, by the President Izetbegovic himself, and if you wish, I can also provide these documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, is Mr Izetbegovic the President of the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina or is he the leader of the Muslim majority, as you put it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was elected President of the 7-member Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina and he was perceived by many people as a leader before he was elected President of this republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, you are testifying here as a scholar, and therefore I think it would be advisable if we should not rely on views of people who saw Izetbegovic as a leader or something else but on the legal documents of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I agree with you on this, but, of course, Alija Izetbegovic existed before he was elected President. How can we then deal with him? How can we take into consideration his writings, his thinking, if we have to call him always President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, I wish to discuss with you the position of Bosnia-Herzegovina as a state regardless of who is its President. Therefore, in connection with your last statement I would like to ask you whether the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the 1974 constitution, with the amendments that you have provided, those of 1989 included, which you have not submitted, nor have you reviewed them -- did it stipulate Bosnia-Herzegovina as a state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that state, both before and after the elections, have its legally-elected bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It had, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina exist as the highest organ of authority in the republic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It existed as a body but it cannot be compared to what it became after 1990 when the first free and multi-party elections were held. You cannot compare these two bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not hear the translation. Can you please repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My answer was that in 1990, when the first free and multi-party elections were held, the institutions of Bosnia were transformed. You cannot compare the institutions after 1990 with the bodies existing before. It's a different thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, that is why I wish to remind you of constitutional amendments of 1989. Were those new bodies constituted in accordance with the constitution of Bosnia Herzegovina and the 1989 amendments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure if I understand your question. Can you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1989 the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina adopted amendments to the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina enabling multi party elections and a multi party system. My question is: since we are talking about the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina whether the bodies elected in 1990 were constitutionally elected state bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The elections in 1990 were multi-party elections, as you were saying, and those were the first free elections held in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Carried out in accordance with the constitution and the elections law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in accordance with the elections law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was no legal discontinuity in the functioning of the institutions of the state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is maybe a legal question, a very specific legal question, and I am not a lawyer. I am a historian. Maybe we can pass this question to a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Ms Calic, today you claimed that after that certain changes occurred in the constitution, certain amendments, which created a confusing situation. Can you explain to us whether you can allege that those legal changes of the constitution in the way envisaged by the constitution could create confusion in a normal state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was referring in my statement to the situation after April 1992. This was after the outbreak of armed conflicts. This was a state of imminent war danger. The Parliament of Bosnia did not function any more. It could not pass any laws any more. These functions were assumed by the state presidency. So the laws were passed by the presidency. It was a different situation, and going through the official gazettes of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1992 I got indeed the impression that many of these regulations were made or were decided on an ad hoc basis. They were reactions to what was happening on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you are familiar with the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina you can probably confirm that the constitution and the laws envisage the procedure for passing laws in conditions of an imminent threat of war and conditions of war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were decrees made by the state Presidency with the effect of laws.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Such decrees were authorised by the constitution in the event of war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore we cannot claim that these decisions could create confusion, because they had legal continuity and a legal basis, do you not think?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry if you understood that they created confusion. I did not intend to say these laws or decrees were creating confusion, but they were made in the middle of a very confusing situation, where many state organs, in fact, did not function any more, and as I was saying before, going through these decrees which were not laws but decrees, going through many of them I got the impression that they were reactions to what was happening on the ground. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Actually if counsel will spare us a little bit, you might avoid conclusions of law in cross-examinations. These are conclusions of law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Actually you have been talking about two different things. You have been talking about the sanction behind the decrees. A sanction is of course a constitution. She is talking about the effect of these laws in the situation, which was very confused at that time. We are talking really about two different matters altogether. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): The situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina I agree is extremely complicated, but I think that Ms Calic can understand me. We are not talking about different things after all. Bosnia-Herzegovina consists in continuity to the present. That is my conclusion. I do not wish to talk about it. I just wish to clarify the conclusions made by Ms Calic in this court. I am not going into constitutional questions any more. Ms Calic, in your paper you claim that the Serb and Croat leaderships wishing to unite their ethnic groups with their motherlands supported the plan for the cantonisation of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the Muslim leadership did not support it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Only for the very short time to be precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I thought the impression you gave to us was this: the Muslim Bosnians wanted to keep the state as a whole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: While the Serbians wanted to split it up and join the rest of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But you said for a short while?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am saying this because in September 1991 the European Union, the European Community, was trying to reconcile these views. They set up this Arbitration Commission and they set up a peace conference, and the situation was very difficult at that time. There were two parties in favour of having ethnic cantons, a federalised state of Bosnia and one party, and the Bosnian government saying: "No, we want to keep it as a unitarian state". So this was a very difficult situation and for a very short moment there appeared to have been agreement between the three parties that -- this was in March 1992 -- that Bosnia could be restructured on the basis of ethnic criteria. This were the so-called "cotilles" or principles, the Foreign Ministry of Portugal mediating between the parties on behalf of the European Community, but immediately afterwards -- this was on 18th March 1992 -- immediately afterwards the Muslim leadership and the Croat leadership seemed to have rejected this plan again, and, in fact, the proposal to create ethnic entries within Bosnia came up again and again in the peace conferences, and, as you can see, today the Dayton Agreement and the constitution of Bosnia of today is also based on ethnic principles. So this was a proposal that was going around since the end of 1991, and some certain moments there was more pressure also from the side of the international community to have these ethnic criteria implemented just to get the situation calm and to come to an agreement. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Ms Calic, in your testimony and the written report you frequently mention the ethnic sides and ethnic leaderships. That is why I am asking you once again: can you confirm that throughout that period there were legally-elected bodies: the Assembly, the Presidency and the Government; regardless of who were members of those bodies and what their percentage share was in those bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can confirm that there were such bodies, but I have also to stress that these bodies did not function as they should have functioned, as they were meant to function, because in October 1991 the Serbs left most of these bodies. So they were just something like rump bodies. All the debate was exactly over this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, can you confirm that all Serbs or members of SDS and SPO walked out of the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If all members walked out of the Assembly, the SDS members walked out of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all Serbs or only members, deputies of SDS and SPO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I was actually talking about political parties, not of nationals, and I also would not intend to consider all Serbs being members of these parties or supporting these parties. Of course not there were many Serbs who did not support these parties and who did not elect them. The same is true for the other parties to the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the President of the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina until Dayton was a Serb, Miro Lazovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two members of the Presidency throughout the war were Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That the national composition of the Presidency did not change, 3, 2, 1, 2, 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why then are you talking of the Muslim leadership all the time then and not referring to the legal authorities of the statement of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This may be again a legal question, and I may be again not be the right person to answer. This legal question was -- I was trying to explain that there was, in fact, legally elected bodies existing in Bosnia-Herzegovina at this time, but on the other hand these bodies were not functioning any more as they were meant to function, and it is maybe just -- you know, there is a difference between what was on paper and what was on the legal side, and then what was in reality, and the reality was that the members of the SDS party which got the majority of Serb votes then left the Assembly and they have left the Presidency, and they did not want to participate any more in the work of this, and unfortunately because of the war there was no possibility to have new elections. We had them as late as September last year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, you were introduced as an expert for political matters. These are not legal; these are political matters. There are legal regulations stipulating how deputies are substituted, those who leave the assembly, those who resign or give up. With the withdrawal of a certain number of deputies from the legal bodies of Bosnia-Herzegovina at least according to the view of the United Nations they did not lose the status of legitimate bodies of authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not intend to say this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but in the course of your testimony and in your written report you constantly repeatedly used the term "Muslim leadership" but, in fact, you were referring to the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina, of which the President throughout the war was a Serb, and many deputies were both Serb and Croat in the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, I did not use Muslim leadership when I was talking about the Presidency, but I used the term "President", "Presidency" many times. However, I used also the term "Muslim leadership" because there were more Muslim leaders than were represented in the presidency. There were local Muslim leaders. I have maybe a problem with language, but I would not like to contest the legitimacy of the Bosnian Presidency. It was a recognised state. I was showing this many times, and I -- yes, it was a recognised state and the President of Bosnia was a recognised President. It was not my intention and I apologise if you got this impression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not talking about an impression. I quoted from your report, and you can confirm what I am saying, and that is the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina had 7 members, of which 3 were Muslim, 2 Serb and 2 Croat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the legality of the highest bodies of authority, can you confirm that they did have the opportunity to lawfully pass decisions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they passed decisions under the circumstances of an immediate threat of war, at least after April 1992, and then from June 1992 onwards under the state of war. These were very specific conditions of this -- yes, very specific conditions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but the state of immediate threat of war is also envisaged by the constitution and other regulations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you said today that one period was a period that could be called a short break or a vacuum in the legal system, are you aware that already in April a decree was passed to take over the regulations of the former SFRY to be implemented in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Does that mean that legal continuity was ensured without interruption?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a certain way, because there were all these amendments coming after this. The Bosnian government had to change, for instance, names. They had to adapt many laws and Articles of the constitution to the changing situation. So there was a basic stock of constitutional Articles, which were continuing to exist but there were also some new, and I was trying to show some of these new decrees, and I was also trying to show some of the old elements or how old elements of the former Yugoslav systems were still existing and how new were introduced. I did not intend to give the impression that this was illegally done. I was just trying to show how the government was trying to adapt to the new conditions and to react to the changing circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly we are not talking about the substance of those acts. We are just saying that this was a legal state that was in existence in continuity as a sovereign and independent state, and as such it passed certain documents in accordance with its own laws and regulations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosnia was indeed recognised on 6th April 1992 by the European Community and afterwards by many other countries and states.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, at the ministerial meeting in Luxembourg, and the following day it was recognised by the United States and Croatia, and on the 8th the first diplomatic relations were established. That is without doubt and you did not dispute that fact, but, Ms Calic, you spoke here about the intentions of the Serb and Croat leaderships from Bosnia and their wish to link up with their motherlands. Are you aware, Ms Calic, that in the former SFRY and in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina there was a law on citizenship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in accordance with that law all citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina who were born there or who belonged to it by origin are citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you consider all citizens of Konjic who, in accordance with this law, were born there or come there by descent are also citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see, it is not up to me to decide these legal questions. I was just trying to explain that part of the Bosnian population, namely a bigger part of the Bosnian Serb population did, in fact, not intend to be considered only as citizens of Bosnia, but they wanted to be considered citizens of Yugoslavia, and whether or not this is a illegal, I cannot say. I am not a legal expert, and also the members of the European Community were a bit confused about this fact, and they had to establish a commission. So I am afraid I cannot answer this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, you agree that there is a citizenship based on laws of the former SRY and Bosnia-Herzegovina and that they regulate this issue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, I will move on to another set of questions. In your presentation and today's testimony you did not speak about other political aspects relating to the aggression on Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you know that over a longer historical -- period of time in history that there are tendencies working towards the destruction of Bosnia-Herzegovina and coming from outside Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no such document available showing a plan to destroy Bosnia as a state. I have indicated that forces from outside Bosnia were involved in the struggle over Bosnia, and this is what I was trying to show in my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you, as a historian, know about Garasanin and his work "Natje Tanja?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the concept of the independent state of Croatian of World War II?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do both of these concepts negate Bosnia-Herzegovina as a state and Bosnia as a nation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far the first concept, the Serb,"Natje Tanja" was made at this time and Bosnia did not exist as an independent state. As for the second one, Bosnia did not exist yet as an independent state before the Second World War. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Now I think the Trial Chamber will rise for 20 minutes. We will assemble at 4.15. (3.55 pm) (Short break) (4.15pm) JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: The witness is still on oath. I think you can carry on with your cross-examination. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honour. Thank you, Ms Calic. I have a number of questions that I need to ask of you. You were talking about the historical continuity. Please can you answer the following questions. Is the geo-political context of Bosnia-Herzegovina also very important for understanding the recent past?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the actual or before the war historically?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The historical context before the war relating to the causes of the war. I asked you earlier and I would like a response: do you know the political treatise of Garasanin, a Serbian politician, called "Natje Tanja"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the political project and territorial framework of the Croatian fascist creation during World War II?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you also familiar with Memorandum of the Serbian Academy of Sciences?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that there was a military plan by the former JNA called Ram and its political underpinnings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was reported in the press. I never seen any document plan Ram.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the names of Greater Serbia and Greater Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Among the documents that I quoted earlier can you identify those that are the political foundation for the Greater Serbia and Greater Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not seen this plan Ram, so I cannot really speak. I saw a press report on it, but I have never seen this plan, so I cannot comment on this. As for the Memorandum of the Serb Academy of Science it is quite unprecise on the territorial side, so I am unable to compare the territorial aspirations of the Natje Tanja document with any assumed territorial aspirations elaborated in this SANU Memorandum. They are not so explicitly formulated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The motto "All Serbs in a single state", is that motto directly or indirectly relating to the security of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not necessarily, because in Yugoslavia the Serbs were living in one state and it was a state where Serbs believed to live together and Bosnia still existed as a republic, had institutions, had its territorial borders. So it is just a matter of interpretation and it is a matter of politics in which concrete shape you then realise the aim: "All Serbs have to live in one state".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you quoted a document speaking about dissolution of Yugoslavia, such a motto can also mean something else with respect to the security of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What can it mean? You mean after the dissolution of Yugoslavia? I cannot understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there is still insistence on all Serbs living in a single state, does that affect directly Bosnia-Herzegovina as well, which is populated by 30 per cent of Serbs, given its ethnic distribution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It affects, of course, Bosnia, but the Serbs, on the other hand, were insisting on the fact that they wanted to remain in Yugoslavia, and the way Yugoslavia dissolved was not correct according to their views. So this is what the Serb position was on this fact, but it affected, of course, the territorial integrity of Bosnia-Herzegovina as a state once it was recognised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your opinion that part of the strategy to create a Greater Serbia is also the quick pull-out of the JNA from Slovenia and Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot -- I do not wish to argue in terms of a plan of Greater Serbia. In Slovenia there were nearly no Serbs living and I would assume also there were no territorial aspirations on the side of the JNA and on the side of Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, keeping the armed forces was only limited to the areas where there were territorial aspirations; is that not what you are stating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am stating that I do not like to argue in terms of plan to create Greater Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can appreciate your desire not to speak of that. We accepted you as an impartial expert with knowledge of political and historical issues, but I am not going to insist on this question. However, I have following questions for you, since you are an expert in this field. Based on your expertise rather than your desires to answer these questions or not, you chose not to answer them. You said that Bosnia was recognised on 6th April 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The decision was taken on 6th April 1992. It came into effect one day later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: as of that moment was the former JNA a foreign military force in the territory of that state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The JNA was after this time still present on the territory of Bosnia. It was then partially withdrawn. Some troops remained, and there remained also support from Belgrade, and I was trying to explain this morning that the bigger part of this JNA was, in fact, transformed into the Bosnian Serb Army, leaving behind troops, leaving behind weaponry and equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: She said that already. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: She was just asking a simple question: was JNA on foreign territory? That is all she asked.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: JNA was on Bosnian territory and it was under the command of Belgrade, superior command of Belgrade. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Does that mean that as of that moment there was an aggression on Bosnia-Herzegovina and it was an international armed conflict from there on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 27th April the new Yugoslavia was created, and I think that from this moment onwards we can consider for sure the JNA as a foreign force being present on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in early May the Security Council brought a Resolution ordering all forces of the JNA to leave Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that this was not done within the deadline of 19th May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that, following that, on 30th May the Security Council introduced sanctions against Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that JNA, the Army of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, through its officer corps, logistics and other ways was continually present in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me if you have the data on the JNA preparing for this aggression over a longer period of time? Do you know that in May of 1991 under the pretence of military exercises all major centres of Bosnia-Herzegovina were blocked with heavy weaponry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that many important strategic points were blocked or controlled by the JNA at this time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sarajevo, Bihac, Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you also know that from 1990 on the weapons legally belonging to the Territorial Defence was kept, guarded by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that these weapons were distributed to the Serbian population of Bosnia-Herzegovina through the SDS and JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know of this. I know that this happened in certain parts, in certain areas in Bosnia, and I also submitted a document to support this view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, the JNA behaved as an aggressor in large portions of the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is probably not correct for the time before Bosnia was recognised as an independent state, and the JNA started distributing weapons a month ago, so I think we have to distinguish between the period before the international recognition of Bosnia and the period after.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I am thinking of the period after. Is the fact that Yugoslavia played this role in Bosnia-Herzegovina one of the reasons why it was not recognised by the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Miss Chalic, I would like to go into the questions relating to the Konjic area. Before that, just one more question relating to the general political issues. In your written report you stated that there were whispers about speculations that the President of Serbia, Milosevic, and President of Croatia, Tudjman, as well as the leader of Bosnian Serbs, Radovan Karadzic, and Bosnian Croats, Mate Boban, had agreed on the partition of Bosnia. Please answer whether there was a meeting between Tudjman and Milosevic in Karageorgevic or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard about this meeting. However, I have never seen any document coming out of this meeting. I included this actually in this paragraph on the speculations on what might have been agreed. So I am aware of this fact, that there was a meeting in Karageorgevic, but I am not aware of the exact outcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in 1990, in June, Mate Boban and Radovan Karadzic met in Graz?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the same. It was reported in the press they met, but we have never seen any documents, any result coming out of these meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are expecting precise data from you as an expert. I think that such an answer based on speculation cannot be part of an expert opinion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I presented what I believed and was reported in the press and I want to make clear I have no exact information of the outcome of these meetings, and these meetings were also behind closed doors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, you offered documents that are results of such agreements. The decisions on creation of the Assembly of Republika Srpska, of the Croatian community Herceg-Bosna, division of the territory, do they not speak about the realisation and results of these agreements, if we disregard all the victims that have come as a result of these agreements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In none of the documents that I have submitted we can find any agreement between Croat -- Croatian and Serbian or Croat and Serb leaders or Presidents or authorities. These documents show how the Serb leaders, on the one hand, and the Croat leaders, on the other hand, were trying to establish autonomous areas, how they were trying to establish quasi-structures, but they cannot show us how the two communities were trying to divide Bosnia between themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion could these states that you have mentioned have been states based on the laws in Bosnia-Herzegovina or were they just para-states?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were para-states, and the Constitutional Court made several decisions that are all included in my file. The Constitutional Court considered the creation of these para-states as unconstitutional in several Decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, before I move on to the Konjic region, I will only say a couple of things. I recognise that you did your doctorate on the social issues in Serbia, that you have been employed in the Institute in Munich, and that you have worked for the German Government, and this is the basis of your knowledge, and the number of documents that you have also submitted. Please if you could tell me what is the basis of your knowledge of the historical, geo-political and military circumstances of the Konjic region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Can you repeat, because I am parallelly listening to the original and the translation and in the middle I lost the connection. Maybe just the translator to repeat the question, if you can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please what documents did you use for -- as a basis for forming your opinion on the Konjic region, and who made these documents available to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I used many documents. I started with the Encyclopedia Yugoslavia. They have a separate volume on Bosnia and there are several pages, several parts also referring to Konjic, especially the parts on the geography, on economy and others. I used then statistical data from the official statistical yearbooks of Yugoslavia, the last one from 1991. I used to a lesser extent press reports. I also used some documents made available to me by the Office of the Prosecutor, and what did I use? I also used some books. I also used books actually, yes. I used the books by Cekic and I used -- yes, this is what I used basically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had no specific personal research, nor did you have insight into documents that would refer specifically to that region except for these indirect documents, indirect sources?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there were the quoted sources which I was using. There were many references to Konjic directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Allow me to say that in your written report you say that: "During the Second World War the region of Konjic witnessed the fiercest ethnic conflicts in Bosnia."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I already know the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in this region the forces of the National Liberation Army, led by Marshall Tito, conducted their Fourth Offensive against the Germans and Italians, together with domestic traitors, the Ustashas and the Cetniks. This was known as "The Battle on the Neretva". A film of that name was nominated for the Oscar award.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you thinking of those events and battles, especially against the Cetniks at Prenj, after crossing the Neretva River when you made this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was also thinking of these battles, but not only, but also of these partisan struggles, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say then that this part of your report is not quite correct when talking about the events during the Second World War in the territory of the municipality of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the area, in the broader area. I was referring to the area. I cannot understand why it is not correct to explain how history developed in this area, and Konjic was part of the Neretva area. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms Calic. You said that these were the fiercest ethnic conflicts, but, in fact, it was a liberation, anti-Fascist movement, against occupation by Fascism. As far as I know, these are quite different legal, historical and political categories.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unfortunately on the side of the German occupation, troops were also fighting troops consisting of Croats and Muslims. These were mainly special forces created by the German SS. The SS was a special force kind of elite troop of the Germans. They were well-known for committing many crimes unfortunately, especially in the second half of this cruel war. Also Croats and Muslims participated in this struggle, some of them voluntarily and some of them were forced, and it remained unfortunately in the memory of many people, and many people perceive it today also as an ethnic struggle, even if the partisan movement as such was a multi-ethnic, pan-Yugoslav movement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you have just said, Ms Calic, is something that you have not written in your report. I accept the explanation, but a host of documentation can be found in the museum in Jablanica. Obviously you have not had occasion to consult that documentation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to this area when I was a student, so this is ten years ago, but I know the monument. I know also much of the history of the partisan struggles. I was a bit brief, but there are many parts in my statement, which was only 13 pages long, in which I could not elaborate all interesting, all relevant information. I confess it is very brief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise for insisting, but you made no mention of the anti-Fascist struggle in this part of your report, but I think we have cleared things up now and I will not insist on further answers to my questions. Can you tell me whether the overall situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina was reflected upon the situation in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I would agree on that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that an event in October 1991 decisively affected and influenced the further course of events in Bosnia-Herzegovina? Let me remind you, and to remind you I would like to show you a brief tape of that event. It maybe takes fifteen seconds. If I may, I would like to call on the Technical Department. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, you are permitted. You can show your tape. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Will you please give the text of the translation? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we please have the text? I cannot hear my sound. There is no sound. Could you repeat the insert, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And I have no pictures. I have nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps this text could be given to the interpreters, so that they can read it. This would avoid having two pictures on the monitor. There is no sound. Will you please read the text if there is an error on the videotape? Will the technicians please try to reproduce the tone? Will you please read the text of this speech in the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How is it relevant? MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): It is important that an expert witness who is dealing with historical events in Bosnia-Herzegovina should identify this man and this Assembly and the words which significantly determined developments, including in the territory of the municipality of Konjic; in the whole state and, of course, also in Konjic. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Let us hear the interpretation, so that you will get what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How do we know that this statement was made by this gentleman on the screen? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Please let us hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The text reads: "You want to take Bosnia-Herzegovina down the same highway to hell and suffering that Slovenia and Croatia are suffering? You do not think that you will lead Bosnia-Herzegovina into hell and do not think that you will not perhaps make the Muslim people disappear because the Muslims cannot defend themselves if there is a war. How will you prevent everyone from being killed in Bosnia-Herzegovina?" Underneath it says: "Radovan Karadzic, Leader of the Bosnian Serbs before the Bosnian-Herzegovina Assembly, October 14, 1991". JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I gather you can now hear the videotape. Let us hear it from the words of the speaker himself. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr President, I would ask the witness to look at the text and to say whether she can recognise the man and is she aware of the words written on this piece of paper as being the words uttered by this man.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I actually had no -- I had only the picture. I had no words, but I am familiar with this document. It is published in the same Cekic book which I was also using. So it is familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you testify before this court who we are talking about and what he said on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not hear the tone. I know the document from the book, but I had no words. I could not -- maybe you can repeat. If I had to translate ... I still have nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can use the text you have before you as a translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What should I -- what did you ask me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking: can you recognise the picture of the man and whether this is what he said at that Assembly meeting, who he is and what he said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised Karadzic on the screen, but I did not get his words because they simply were not in my earphones, I am afraid, but I know this document from the Cekic book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the BBC programme too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe. I have it in my mind that I have read it in this Cekic book. This is where I ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. Did the court hear the words spoken by the person? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I did not hear it. I heard the interpretation. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I would like to ask the witness to testify, having said that she knows that it was Radovan Karadzic in the Assembly of Herzegovina and that she is aware of the words he spoke on that occasion, can she testify that those words had a decisive effect on the further course of events in Bosnia-Herzegovina? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I do not think she can testify to that. She was not a member of the Assembly. She had nothing other than what any other person observed. So how do you expect her to testify to that? If you have other questions, more valid questions, please try and put them to her. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honour, she is not a factual witness. She is Ms Calic, an expert, and we are asking to testify to a document from the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina which was shown before this court on several occasions, and if she can confirm that document, I would like to ask her to do so. If not, I would be grateful if she looked at it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot confirm this, because I have not seen this tape before, not here in the court. I know this document from publication, from the Cekic book, as I was saying, but I am not a fact witness. I did not attend this meeting, and I could unfortunately not understand from my earphones what Karadzic was saying here on this tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you testify what the document in Cekic's book says that you are familiar with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have a big problem with translating and I had it already when I read it for the first time in this book. It concerns the word "disappear". I cannot exactly remember the Bosnian word, so I am afraid I have not the original text and I am not a fact witness, but if this is important, we can provide the book. We can find the book or we can make the screen work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this word "disappear" apply to the Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot testify on this, I am afraid.
