utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the book written, please, so that defence could perhaps submit it as evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1993. We have it here. I think I brought a copy, but I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, can you tell us please whether you know that the town of Konjic after these events was blocked as an important strategic point along the line from Sarajevo to the sea?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm again not a fact witness. I read in some of the witnesses' reports that the road was blocked, but I personally am not capable of confirming or not confirming this fact. I'm not a fact witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that already on 29th April an air raid was announced and actually carried out at the point of Glavicine, Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again I am not a fact witness, and I personally did not witness any of these attacks, so it would be maybe better to ask these questions to the fact witnesses and not to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, I am still asking you a question as an expert. You said that you could testify on events in the region of Konjic. In answer to each of my questions you say that you are not a fact witness. I am not expecting you to say that you lived in Konjic, but as an expert you could have had the opportunity to study documents relating to these events.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had the opportunity to study documents on these events, but I am not sure to which extent I can rely on each of these documents, and I really would prefer that you asked these questions to the fact witnesses and not to me, because I was asked to give a general background to help the court to place into context what was going on, but I was not asked to testify on these facts, and I am afraid that I am incapable of doing this, because I was not present in the area at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The war, the bombing raids and all the other events that I am mentioning are historical events, and you are an expert on history. Can you confirm that from May 4th Konjic was daily exposed to terrible raids? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Please can I advise counsel: you started very well by outlining what the witness came to say, historical, geographic context in which the whole event occurred, but specific events or daily happenings might be something of history, but it is not a history preceding what has happened. I do not think the witness is in a position to be answering specific questions of bombing raids. That is not the reason why the expert was asked to come and testify. It has nothing to do with this case. In fact, that is not even a question of expertise. There is no expertise in knowing there was a bomb raid, whether a place was bombed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Perhaps you can ask her was the area generally bombarded. Maybe about that she might be knowing, but not specific raids, or blockades. She said earlier many places were blockaded. Maybe Konjic was also one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In this general way I can confirm. I also submitted a report by the UNHCR, which gives evidence of this. Many, many houses and other buildings were destroyed during the war. I, of course, cannot say which specific raid or which specific bombing or shooting was then the real event, because there was, of course, also afterwards fighting in this area, fighting between also Croat and Muslim forces. So in the general way I can confirm there were many attacks on Konjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Bombing raids?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also bombing raids. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, I apologise, but in the announcement to the defence it was indicated to us that Ms Calic would be speaking about concrete historic, political, economic and military questions of importance for the region of Konjic, and I am really confused if I cannot ask Ms Calic questions about the subjects that I was told she would be testifying to. I did not ask about any particular building. The month of May was an important historical period, when within half an hour there were 44 air raids. I am not asking her that, but whether Konjic was exposed to heavy shelling. In our view and from the standpoint of that region it is a political and military and historical fact. So, if possible, I would like her to answer this question. If she is aware of it, then let her tell me so, and if she does not know, she does not know. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I am sorry if you are getting a little worried, and I do not want to be tedious about such things. Now when an expert comes to give evidence about historical incidents or things leading towards anything, the expert is not a participant observer and is not expected to give evidence of what happened during the conflict. So I do not see how you can go as far as that. I suppose if the Prosecution does not object, I think you can go ahead asking whatever questions you like, but I think that is not the way to conduct a cross-examination of an expert. I am not talking about somebody who was a participant. When you are asking an expert questions, you know your limits. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honours. The expert has just told us that she had many sources of the United Nations and other agencies about the heavy shelling of Konjic, so she could have said that at the beginning. I wish to ask the following question: do you know that from April 1991 there was a significant movement of the population from Eastern Bosnia and Eastern Herzegovina after a terrible crime of ethnic cleansing was committed against the Borciac people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. Did you say 1991 or 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1992. There are many reports again by international experts, like the final report of the UN Commission of Experts, that give evidence on population movements, and I think there can be now no doubt about this fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that tens of thousands of people from those regions were moving over the Bosnian mountains towards Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As an expert, is it your opinion that this situation affected significantly the political and other situation in the Konjic municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, and we could see this also afterwards in the following years, when masses of refugees and displaced persons were moving to Central Bosnia, which was a matter of concern, of course, with the local authorities, and it created conflicts between Muslims and Croats over the division of resources and everything else. I agree this was a real matter of concern. I mentioned it actually at the end of my report, that there were about 8,000 people coming to Konjic, new people coming to Konjic, displaced persons from other areas, mainly from Eastern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this number of 8,000 could also be much higher, or do you allow that possibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really don't know. I rely here on a report by UNHCR, which is in my opinion a reliable source, and I personally cannot speculate whether there was a higher number or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a social scientist, can you confirm that such events and such movements of people were creating enormous difficulties to the authorities in that region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving to the last group of questions that I would like to ask you, and I thank you for your patience in answering what you are able to answer, as far as the structures of authorities in the Konjic area are concerned, I would like to know whether you had access to the documents relating to the local government in Konjic, the document relating to the Assembly of Konjic and then the decisions that were taken later, and if you can give me the sources of your information in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had unfortunately only some of these documents available. I was -- I requested them and, as I understand, the Office of the Prosecutor was also trying to get them, but unfortunately the Bosnian institutions -- I do not know which institution it was -- were not able to provide them in time, but we are trying -- keep on trying to get these documents. I don't know for which reason it was not possible to get them from Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You submitted a document on the all people's defence strategy issued by the Federal Ministry for Defence of SFRY. Do you know that on 10th April the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina issued a Directive regarding organising and operating of the staffs of Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the date?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 10th April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Also the year. 10th April 1992? Please repeat the year also. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. Can you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that on 10th April a Provisional Directive was issued, in which a reorganisation of the local headquarters were put in a new hierarchical order towards the General Command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If this is the one published in the Official Gazette, yes. If it's a secret one, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is not the Directive that you submitted in your documents. Were you in a position to see another document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I submitted two documents relating to the Bosnian Army and the Territorial Defence Organisation. Both were passed in May 1992. One is the Defence Law of Bosnia. The other one is the law on the armed forces, and both laws are included in this binder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, you did not see other documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw the whole Official Gazette. If you are referring to documents published in this Gazette related to defence, I have seen them. If you are speaking about whatever secret decisions internally made, I have not seen them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw the Decree in the Official Gazette taking over the laws from the former SFRY?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw that a number of documents were taken over, but not documents relating to the defence matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the Bosnian Government was passing new documents, but they were, in my view, very similar to the former ones in essence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Bosnian government did not adopt this strategy of all people's defence and self-protection of the people, did it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This strategy was in effect on the Republics of the former Yugoslavia, and I actually did get it from the Republic of the former Yugoslavia, whose name is not Serbia or Montenegro, and I was advised by former Attorney-General that it was still valid at this time and that many military persons were still behaving according to this defence doctrine, and my general impression from what was going on on the ground is indeed that many people still behaved in accordance with this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not personally verify the actions or behaviour of the people in the Konjic municipality, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not. I was saying it before, that I am not a fact witness. I cannot confirm or not confirm any concrete behaviour of any person at this time in the area of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, you have confirmed certain things in your written report. You stated that there was a rule or frequent cases that people of some standing, people who had money, people who were businessmen, were coming to help their people, and you stated examples in Croatia and Bosnia. Do you think you can cite five such persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not like to cite five such persons. I cited two prominent persons and I think, if you give me a bit more time, I will find other adequate examples. I quoted a bit earlier the case of Arkan and I quoted the case of Fikret Abdic. I think I can also maybe find some more, but I would need a bit more time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. Arkan is not a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I am not sure that I know in what context you used him here, and Fikret Abdic did not come from abroad. Based on these two individuals I don't know how you arrived at the conclusion that you arrived at in your written report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, both persons were acting on the territory of Bosnia and both persons were also relying on financial resourcing coming from outside of Bosnia. I, of course, have no documents here, and I am, of course, again not a witness, a fact witness for this, but this is what was generally assumed at the time, and I think many still believe in this, and they were powerful persons just because they had a lot of economic power in certain areas, one in Western Bosnia and the other one in Eastern Slovenia. They had the bases and they had good contacts outside of the Republic of Bosnia and outside of also Croatia and they had connections to foreign countries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, those are not individuals who are the members of the legal armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they are not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, what you testified to in your written report does not refer to the members of the legal armed forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not mention the armed forces of Bosnia in this context, if I remember well. If you understand this, then I apologise. It was not my intention to put it in such a way. I wanted just to say that in a situation where really everything was changing, it was a normal thing that new elites were emerging, persons of influence were coming in. Immigrants were coming back from foreign countries. This was not only the case in Bosnia, but also in Serbia and Croatia and maybe also in the other republics. It was maybe part of this -- excuse me again -- confused situation, which is, I was trying to explain, this confused situation which characterised the first months after the outbreak of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, a little while ago you correctly pointed to the fact that you were not a fact witness. I would like to ask you: is this your assumption or is it a historical fact that you got based on the information available to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which fact are you referring to, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact about influential persons who were coming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it has become already a historical fact, and there are scholars who have written about this. I have a chapter of a book by a French scholar. His name is Xavier Bugarel. The article is not included in this file, because I thought it would not be relevant for this case, but I can provide you with this book and with this article. So there are already scholars writing about this fact, and I think we should also take notice of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms Calic, but you are testifying about the Konjic area, and you testified that these people were business people, cafe owners, who were supporting certain political parties, who provided financial resources to them, and who also had influence on political and military structures, especially in the area of 1992/1992. This is what is in the indictment, that period, and in the beginning of this paragraph we are talking about Bosnia-Herzegovina, including the Konjic area, and I am asking you whether you have facts that are -- information that is based on facts or are you just referring to general books and other general documents when stating this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, then I did not mention in this report Konjic specifically. I was mentioning Bosnia as a part of the former Yugoslavia, and I would like to stress here again that this is also true for many other parts of the former Yugoslavia. It was a general fact. It happened in many parts. It happened on all sides, I would assume, and there are already scholars writing on these facts, and this is what I wanted to make clear here. I was not, of course, as I am not a fact witness, referring to a concrete person or concrete -- yes, a concrete person in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was an assumption on your part that it also was referring to the Konjic area; can we put it that way?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this question. You are putting something else in the mouth of the witness. The witness just said that it was not in the Konjic area. It was a general observation. The question is answered already. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Well, the witness actually said that she had no such experience with the facts surrounding the Konjic area. Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I have no facts or evidence personally. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honour, but the paragraph that I just quoted starts with the words: "In all parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina including Konjic ...". So I could not understand it in any other way but the way it is written. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: If she has now made that exception of the place which you have in mind, you ought to accept that. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you. The next group of short questions is in reference to your knowledge of the structures in the Konjic municipality. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I am sorry. You might not have enough time for these short questions, because we have to rise at 5.30. So you might continue tomorrow morning at 10.00 am. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you very much. Thank you, Ms Calic. (Court adjourned until 10.30 tomorrow morning) --ooOoo-- 25
